warnings.description: `token_scope_broader_than_zone`: the token could see other zones; revoke it now. `partially_applied`: some records were written and some failed (see each item's `error`).

zone.description: The provider zone the records go in.

apply_providers.description: Providers `POST …/apply` can set the records up with for this zone. Empty when the zone is at a provider we cannot write to: publish the records by hand or download them with `…/export`.

callback_urls.description: Once active: the OAuth redirect URLs on this host. A sign-in started on the custom host returns to it, so add these to each provider's app next to the existing ones. Null while not active.

dns_provider.description: Who hosts the zone, from its nameservers.

dns_zone.description: The DNS zone holding the host, when it could be found.

records.description: The two records to publish, routing first.

serving.description: True when the host serves this app right now: the domain is `active` and custom domains are switched on for the workspace.

status.description: `pending`: waiting for both records. `active`: both records are published; the host serves this app's sign-in routes. `failing`: was active, and a later check no longer finds the records. verified_at.description: When the domain last became active.

available.description: True when custom domains are switched on for this app's workspace, so `POST` can add one. While the feature is in early access it is switched on per workspace; when false, adding a domain answers 403 `FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED`.

data.description: An app has at most one custom domain.

name.description: The name relative to the DNS zone, as most DNS provider forms want it (`@` for the zone itself).

observed.description: What the name serves for this record type at the last check.

purpose.description: `routing`: the CNAME that sends the host to our edge. `ownership`: the TXT token that proves the domain is yours.

state.description: `verified`: public DNS serves it. `propagating`: your DNS provider serves it, public resolvers not yet (usually minutes). `not_found`: not published yet. `conflict`: something at the name blocks it (see `conflicts`). `lookup_failed`: DNS did not answer; the next check tries again.

verified_at.description: First check that found the record, since it was last missing.

code.description: Why the record cannot work as things stand. `cname_foreign`: the name already points somewhere else. `records_at_cname_host`: the name holds A, MX or TXT records, and a CNAME cannot share its name. `cname_at_host`: the TXT name is itself a CNAME.

message.example: auth.acme.com already points at acme.netlify.app. Change that CNAME to edge.auth.productcraft.co, or use another name.

severity.description: `blocking`: the record cannot be published until this is fixed. `warning`: it works, but read the message.

suggested_value.description: The value to publish instead, when there is one.

id.description: Provider id from the zone's nameservers (`cloudflare`, `digitalocean`, `route53`, `godaddy`, … or `other`).

address.description: The From Auth emails go out with: a bare address or `Name <address>`. null when none is set (no workspace default in Mail yet, or `custom` with no address), and also when the workspace default could not be read (`verified: null`).

domain_status.description: The sender domain's live `verification_status` in Mail (`verified`, `pending`, `temporary_failure`, `failed`, …), `deleted` when the domain behind the workspace default was removed, `not_found` for a custom address on no sending domain of this workspace, or null when unknown or there is no address. source.description: `workspace`: the workspace default sender set in Mail. `custom`: this app's own `default_sender_address`.

verified.description: Whether mail from this sender goes out right now, checked live in Mail. false: the domain is not verified, no sender is set, or a custom address is on no domain of this workspace. null: not checked (your role cannot read Mail, or Mail did not answer).

code_expires_at.description: Expiry of the emailed enrollment code (self-service enrollment only).

email_masked.description: Masked address the enrollment code was sent to.

count.description: Rows with this action in the user's whole history.

ip.description: Client IP recorded on the row.

resource_id.description: Id of the resource, when there is one.

action_counts.description: Whole history by action, most frequent first.

activity.description: Most recent audit entries, newest first (capped).

activity_truncated.description: True when `activity` hit its cap and older rows exist.

no_activity_recorded.description: True when the user has no audit row at all ("nothing recorded"), as opposed to an empty page.

window_days.description: Window, in days, every in-window figure covers.

code.description: Invite code the recipient submits to accept.

role_name.description: Role name now bound to the app membership.

user_id.description: Account UUID of the end-user whose role changed.

auth_methods.description: Authentication methods used to establish the session.

mfa_at.description: When an MFA step completed on this session.

auth_providers.description: How this person can sign in: `password` when a credential exists, plus each linked OAuth provider (`google`, `apple`, …). Empty means neither — an admin-created account that has not been sent a password reset cannot get in at all, and that is a real state rather than missing data.

failed_signins.description: Failed sign-ins in the last 30 days. Flagged at 3.

last_activity_at.description: Most recent audit-log entry with this user as the actor. Null means we have never recorded them doing anything — which is a different fact from "no session", and the one that tells you whether they ever got in.

step_up_locked_until.description: Set while a live session is locked out of step-up verification.

verified_email_count.description: Verified email contacts, primary or not. Distinct from `emailVerifiedAt`, which is the primary contact only — the `unverified` filter accepts any verified email, so a renderer branching on `emailVerifiedAt` would disagree with it.

data.description: Deduplicated set of `<resource>.<action>` permission strings that at least one Consumer-API route gates via `@RequireAppPermission`. App-agnostic — the same users-api binary serves every app, so the set does not vary by `:appId`. Lets the console surface an "Enforced" badge so customers can tell which catalog entries do real work.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable error code; branch on this, not on `message`. Always present. A route-specific code when the route defines one (e.g. `WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND`, `SERVICE_NOT_ENABLED`), otherwise the generic code for the status: `BAD_REQUEST`, `VALIDATION_ERROR` (400 from request validation), `UNAUTHORIZED`, `FORBIDDEN`, `NOT_FOUND`, `CONFLICT`, `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, `UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`.

message.description: Human-readable error message. May be a class-validator array on 400.

statusCode.description: HTTP status code echoed in the body. Spelled `statusCode` (camelCase) in every ProductCraft API.

code.description: The opaque `heimdall_code` the customer received on the OAuth callback `return_to`. Single-use; expires after 60 seconds.

access_token.description: Present on the ordinary sign-in outcome. Absent when `mfa_enrollment_required` is true — no session was minted.

expires_in.description: Lifetime of the access token in seconds.

mfa_enrollment_required.description: Set when the app runs `auth_config.mfa: "required"` and the account holds no enabled factor. NO session was minted; the token fields are absent and `mfa_token` carries the enrolment challenge instead.

mfa_token.description: Enrolment challenge token. Drive `POST /{app_slug}/v1/auth/mfa/enroll` then `/auth/mfa/enroll/verify` with it to enrol a factor and receive tokens. Session-equivalent — treat it like a refresh token and never place it in a URL.

description.description: Shown to the person creating a key.

mfa_token.description: Single-use enrolment token. Not an access token: no session has been created. Complete via `POST /{app_slug}/v1/auth/mfa/enroll` then `/auth/mfa/enroll/verify`.

id_token.description: Provider-issued ID token (JWT). For Apple, the value returned by `ASAuthorizationAppleIDCredential.identityToken` after UTF-8 decoding the data.

nonce.description: Raw nonce the client generated and SHA-256-hashed into the authorize request. Backend recomputes the hash and compares to the token's `nonce` claim. Must be at least 32 bytes of entropy (base64url-encoded ~43 chars).

user.description: Apple-specific first-signin payload: { name, email }. Persist for display only — the verified JWT is the source of truth.

expires_in.description: Lifetime of the access token in seconds.

mfa_enrollment_due_at.description: Present only when the app runs `mfa: "required"`, the user holds no enabled factor, and the account is still inside `mfa_grace_days` of its creation. Tokens ARE issued; this is the deadline after which federated sign-in starts returning `mfa_enrollment_required` instead.

line.description: 1-based line number in the uploaded NDJSON. -1 marks the truncation notice.

error_message.description: Set when the JOB itself aborted, as opposed to a row failing.

status.description: `succeeded` means the job ran to completion, not that every row landed — read `failed_count`.

adoption_rate.description: `users_with_factor / users.total`, 0–1. Null when the app has no users.

by_type.description: End users with an enabled factor, by factor type (a user with two types counts in both).

users_with_factor.description: End users with at least one enabled factor.

completed.description: Password resets completed in the window.

requested.description: Password resets requested in the window.

active.description: Sessions that are neither revoked nor expired.

with_mfa.description: Sessions with a completed MFA step (`mfa_at` set), whether or not still active.

failure_rate.description: `failed / (success + failed)`, 0–1. Null when there were no attempts.

active_in_window.description: End users who were the actor of at least one audit event in the window.

new_in_window.description: End users created in the window.

completion_rate.description: `completed / requested`, 0–1. Null when nothing was requested.

token.description: The access token to introspect. Optional — when omitted the endpoint introspects the `Authorization: Bearer` token. When present, it must match the bearer (we refuse cross-token introspection so a stolen token cannot be probed against a different active credential).

token_type_hint.description: Optional `token_type_hint` per RFC 7662. We only issue access tokens at this endpoint so the only meaningful value is `access_token`; the field is accepted for client-library compatibility.

active.description: Per RFC 7662: `true` if the token is currently active for this app, `false` otherwise. An inactive response is the default for any token we can't validate — invalid signature, expired, revoked / expired / deleted session, wrong app — and intentionally carries no other claims so an attacker can't probe the token's shape.

aid.description: App UUID this token is bound to.

iss.description: Issuer URL — the public Auth API base joined with this app slug. Pin this in your local JWKS verifier so a token minted for another app on the platform cannot pass.

scope.description: Space-separated `scope` string per OAuth 2.0 RFC 6749 — alias of `scopes` joined with " ".

sub.description: Subject claim: M2M client id or EndUser account id.

key.description: The tenant API key your API received (`pctk_live_…` / `pctk_test_…`). Sent in the body, never a header. Anything that is not a well-formed key of this app is simply `{"active": false}`.

account_id.description: End user who created (or last rotated) the key.

tenant_role.description: The creator's CURRENT role in the tenant, read live. Intersect `scopes` with this role's permissions in your app: drift can only narrow access.

pagination.description: Always one page (an endpoint limit applies).

client_secret.description: Plaintext client secret. Returned exactly once.
New plaintext client secret. Returned exactly once.

org_role.description: Tenant-scoped role name from the token when signed into a tenant. `null` otherwise.

permissions.description: Sorted union of the app-level role permissions and the tenant-scoped role permissions when applicable.

role.description: App-level role name from the EndUser's token. `null` when unset.

avatar_url.description: Stable avatar URL (`/:appSlug/v1/avatars/:accountId`) when the user has an avatar — uploaded, or captured from a Google/GitHub sign-in. `null` when no avatar exists. Does not expire; each hit 302s to a short-lived presigned URL (or the provider URL).

created_at.description: When the account row was created.

email.description: Primary email contact value. `null` if the user has no email contact.

email_verified_at.description: When the primary email was verified. `null` until verification completes.

joined_at.description: When the EndUser joined the app.

role.description: App-level role name. Resolves per-request from the JWT.

is_current.description: True iff this is the session backing the current request.

pagination.description: { next_cursor, has_more } — pagination fixed to a single page.

metadata.description: Free-form metadata blob stored on the account row.

seq_id.description: Monotonic per-table sequence id (Postgres int8, serialized as a string).

from.description: The From it went out with (the workspace default sender or the app's custom address).

message_id.description: The Mail message id; look it up in Mail > Emails to follow delivery.

template_name.description: The Mail template that was sent.

to.description: Your own verified account address: tests only ever go to the person who asked.

access_token.description: Access token (RS256 JWT signed with the app JWKS key).

heimdall_admin_users_endpoint.description: Customer-product admin lane root. M2M-callable user CRUD.

heimdall_authorize_endpoint.description: Auth-specific authorize endpoint. Not part of standard OIDC.

heimdall_verify_endpoint.description: Auth-specific verify endpoint. Not part of standard OIDC.

issuer.description: Token `iss` claim — the Auth API base URL with the app slug appended. Pin this literally in your verifier so a token minted for another app on the platform cannot pass.

jwks_uri.description: Issuer-aligned JWKS URL — exactly `issuer + '/.well-known/jwks.json'`, which is what OIDC Discovery §4 relying parties expect. The older `/<slug>/v1/.well-known/jwks.json` alias serves the identical document and is not going away.

userinfo_endpoint.description: OIDC userinfo equivalent — returns the signed-in EndUser profile.

has_more.description: True iff another page exists; if true, pass `next_cursor` on the next request.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. `null` when no more pages are available.

config.description: PARTIAL provider config. Only top-level keys present here are changed; omitted keys — secrets included — keep their stored values, so you can update e.g. an Apple service_id without re-uploading the private key. The merged result is validated by the provider impl's `parseConfig` before storage.

enabled.description: Flip the provider live/inactive without touching config.

description.description: Free-text description of what this permission allows.

created_by.description: Who created (or last rotated) the key.

created_by_account_id.description: End user who created (or last rotated) the key. The key dies when they leave the tenant.

key_prefix.description: First 16 characters of the key (environment prefix plus 6). The rest is never retrievable.

rotated_from.description: On a replacement key, the id of the key it replaced.

status.description: `revoked` (wins over everything), `expired`, `orphaned` (neither, but the creator is no longer a member of the tenant or the tenant is not `active`, so introspection answers `{"active": false}`), or `active`. The app-wide kill switch (`suspended` in the config) is not reflected per key.

default_expiry_days.description: Lifetime when the creator names none. At most `max_expiry_days`.

enabled.description: Turn tenant API keys on for this app. Needs at least one grantable scope.

grantable_scopes.description: The scopes a key of this app can carry. Replaces the stored list. At most 64, unique.

manage_roles.description: Tenant roles (this app's role names, case-insensitive) whose members may create, rotate and revoke keys. Default `['owner']`.

management_lane.description: `direct`: an end user's bearer alone can manage keys. `app_proxy_only`: the bearer is accepted only together with this app's PAK in `X-Heimdall-App-Key`, so every change passes through your backend.

max_expiry_days.description: Longest lifetime a key may have.

require_recent_mfa_minutes.description: When set, creating or rotating a key needs a second factor verified within this many minutes. `null` switches it off.

suspended.description: Platform kill switch: while `true`, introspection answers `{"active": false}` for every key of this app and key management is refused with 403 `TENANT_API_KEYS_SUSPENDED`. Only this route sets it; the app's own config push cannot change it.

api_keys_active.description: API keys across those apps. Rows are hard-deleted on revoke so existence implies active.

apps.description: Auth apps the caller is a member of (any role).

callback_url.description: The exact redirect (callback) URL to register at the provider for this app.

provider_error.description: The provider's own OAuth error code from its token endpoint (`invalid_client`, `incorrect_client_credentials`, `invalid_grant`, `redirect_uri_mismatch`, …), or null when it gave none. GitHub answers an unknown client id with a plain 404; that is reported as `unknown_client`. `redirect_uri_mismatch` with `credentials_valid` means the client is right but the redirect URI registered at the provider is not `callback_url`.

result.description: `credentials_valid`: the provider recognised the client id and secret (it only refused the dummy sign-in code we sent). `credentials_rejected`: the provider does not accept the client id or secret; sign-in with this provider is blocked until they are fixed. `inconclusive`: the provider could not be reached or gave an answer we cannot read; nothing is blocked.

config.description: Customer-safe view of the stored config. Public identifiers and metadata only — secrets (Apple private key, Google client secret, …) NEVER appear in the response. `private_key_present: true` is the only acknowledgement that a key is on file.

last_check_at.description: When the credential check last ran. Null until it has run for the saved credentials.

last_check_error.description: The provider's OAuth error code from the last check, if any.

last_check_result.description: Result of the last credential check (run on every save and on `POST …/{provider}/check`). `credentials_valid`: the provider recognised the client id and secret (it only refused the dummy sign-in code we sent). `credentials_rejected`: the provider does not accept the client id or secret; sign-in with this provider is blocked until they are fixed. `inconclusive`: the provider could not be reached or gave an answer we cannot read; nothing is blocked.

blocked_reasons.description:
Why sign-in with this provider fails. Empty when `status` is `ready` or `not_configured`. For a `disabled` provider it lists what would block sign-in once switched on.

- `no_redirect_origins`: The app has no allowed redirect origins, so web sign-in is refused. Add the origin of the site that starts sign-in (for example `https://app.example.com`) under Redirect origins.
- `missing_credentials`: The stored provider credentials are incomplete or can no longer be read. Save the client id and secret (or Apple key) again.
- `credentials_rejected`: The provider rejected the stored credentials the last time they were checked. Copy the client id and secret again from the provider console.

configured.description: True if there is a config row for this (app, provider).

enabled.description: True only when configured AND the row is enabled. Sign-in attempts against an unconfigured / disabled provider return 503.

last_check_at.description: When the credential check last ran. Null until it has run for the saved credentials.

last_check_error.description: The provider's OAuth error code from the last check, if any.

last_check_result.description: Result of the last credential check (run on every save and on `POST …/{provider}/check`). `credentials_valid`: the provider recognised the client id and secret (it only refused the dummy sign-in code we sent). `credentials_rejected`: the provider does not accept the client id or secret; sign-in with this provider is blocked until they are fixed. `inconclusive`: the provider could not be reached or gave an answer we cannot read; nothing is blocked.

status.description: Whether people can sign in with this provider right now, computed on the server with the same rule the web sign-in flow enforces. `ready`: switched on and nothing blocks sign-in. `blocked`: switched on, but sign-in fails until every `blocked_reasons` entry is fixed. `disabled`: configured but switched off. `not_configured`: no credentials saved for this provider.

type.description: Factor type — `totp` (authenticator app), `email` (single-use code delivered to a verified email contact), or `webauthn` (a passkey). Further factor types will extend this list without a breaking change to the response shape.

default_expiry_days.description: Lifetime when the creator names none. At most `max_expiry_days`.

enabled.description: Turn tenant API keys on for this app. Needs at least one grantable scope.

grantable_scopes.description: The scopes a key of this app can carry. Replaces the stored list. At most 64, unique.

manage_roles.description: Tenant roles (this app's role names, case-insensitive) whose members may create, rotate and revoke keys. Default `['owner']`.

management_lane.description: `direct`: an end user's bearer alone can manage keys. `app_proxy_only`: the bearer is accepted only together with this app's PAK in `X-Heimdall-App-Key`, so every change passes through your backend.

max_expiry_days.description: Longest lifetime a key may have.

require_recent_mfa_minutes.description: When set, creating or rotating a key needs a second factor verified within this many minutes. `null` switches it off.

attempts.description: One attempt per endpoint it was sent to.

factors_disabled.description: How many enabled factors were disabled. Zero when the account already held none — the call still destroys recovery codes and revokes sessions.

is_system.description: Whether this is a system role (owner / admin / member).
Whether this is a system role (owner / admin / member).

grace_hours.description: How long the OUTGOING key keeps working, in hours. `0` kills it immediately. Capped at 168 (7 days) — a rotation answers "this key may be compromised", so an unbounded overlap would defeat the point. Rotation can only ever shorten a key: if the old key was already due to expire sooner, that earlier instant stands.

expires_at.description: When this key stops authenticating. `null` means it never expires.

key.description: Raw API key. Returned exactly once — store it now.

key_prefix.description: First 16 chars of the key — safe to display in lists.

previous_key_expires_at.description: When the replaced key stops authenticating. Until then BOTH keys work, so a fleet can roll over without downtime.

rotated_from.description: Id of the key this one replaces.

expires_in_days.description: Lifetime of the replacement in days (7, 30, 90, 365, capped by the app's maximum). Defaults to the original key's window.

grace_hours.description: How long the OUTGOING key keeps working, in hours (0-24). `0` (the default) revokes it immediately. Rotation never lengthens the outgoing key. To get rid of a leaked key, revoke it instead.
Hours the previous secret keeps signing too (0 ends it now).

event_type.description: Which event to send; its catalogue example is the `data`.

permissions.description: Array of permission strings in resource.action format
Permission strings in resource.action format to assign as scopes

detail.description: One or two plain sentences: what is true now and, when the row is not `pass`, what to do about it.
detail.example: No site is allowed to start sign-in, so web sign-in is refused. Add the origin of your site, for example https://app.example.com.

fix.description: Where to fix this row. Null when there is nothing to do or no single place to do it.

id.description: Stable row identifier. Safe to key UI state on; new rows may be added.

state.description: `pass`: done. `attention`: works, but worth a look (not blocking). `not_set`: a required step has not been started. `blocked`: set up, but something stops it from working until it is fixed.

test.description: A real test that proves this row works, when the product offers one. Null otherwise.

href.description: Console-relative path of the exact place to fix this row (may carry a `#section` anchor). Link to it directly; it is never an absolute URL.

label.description: Button text for the fix, in plain words.

action.description: Identifier of the test the console runs for this row (for example `webhook.test` or `sign_in.try`). The product documents each action next to the route that performs it.

label.description: Button text for the test, in plain words.

checked_at.description: When the server computed these rows.

complete.description: True when no row is `not_set` or `blocked`. `attention` rows do not stop setup from being complete.

rows.description: Checklist rows in the order they should be shown.

callback_host.description: The custom domain the test runs on (`custom_domain: true`), or null for the canonical host. The start link is on this host and the provider is sent its callback URL, `https://<callback_host>/v1/auth/oauth/<provider>/callback`.

email_delivery.description: Succeeded `password` / `otp` tests: whether the email went out. A `password` test passes even when it did not, because real sign-up and sign-in do not need it; `notice` says why and how to turn it on. Null for `oauth` tests and failed tests.

expires_at.description: The start link works until then (10 minutes).

outcome.description: What a real sign-in would have done: sign in an existing user, or create a new one. The test itself never creates or links an account.

start_url.description: OAuth tests only: open this in a popup to sign in at the provider. Works once, until `expires_at`. Null once used, for password and email-code tests, and when the test already failed its checks.

state.description: `pending`: waiting for the sign-in at the provider (open `start_url`). `succeeded`: the sign-in would work; see `outcome` and `identity`. `failed`: see `error` for the fix. A test that is never finished becomes `failed` with code `expired`.

notice.description: Why the email did not go out; null when it was sent.

sent.description: True when the verification (or sign-in code) email went to your address.

fix.description: What to do to send it.
fix.example: Optional. To send new users a verification email, turn on emails under the app's Email settings and choose a sender.

message.description: Why the email did not go out, in plain words.
message.example: Sign-up and sign-in work, but no verification email is sent: emails are switched off for this app.

code.description: Codes include the provider's own OAuth error (`redirect_uri_mismatch`, `invalid_client`, `unauthorized_client`, `access_denied`, `invalid_scope`, `invalid_grant`, GitHub `incorrect_client_credentials` / `bad_verification_code`) and ours: `invalid_private_key`, `unknown_client`, `token_invalid`, `provider_not_configured`, `missing_credentials`, `no_redirect_origins`, `link_required`, `account_exists_with_different_provider`, `signup_disabled`, `signin_disabled`, `email_domain_not_allowed`, `operator_email_unavailable`, `emails_off`, `email_sender_missing`, `email_template_missing`, `email_workspace_missing`, `email_unavailable`, `email_send_failed`, `expired`. An unknown provider code is passed through as is.

fix.description: Exactly what to do. Where the fix is a URL to paste into the provider console, the exact URL is included.
fix.example: In Google Cloud console (APIs & Services → Credentials), add this exact URL as an authorized redirect URI, then try again: https://api.auth.productcraft.co/acme/v1/auth/oauth/google/callback

message.description: What went wrong, in plain words.
message.example: Google does not accept our callback URL for this app.

email.description: The email the provider reported, or yours for a password / email-code test.

provider.description: How this person signed in: the provider id (`google`, `github`, `apple`), `password`, or `email_code`.

subject.description: For a provider: the provider's stable user id (`sub`). For a password or email-code test: the id of the existing user with your email in this app, or null when one would be created.

contact_id.description: Email factors only: id of the verified email contact the codes should be delivered to. Defaults to the primary verified email. 412 when the contact (or the primary email) is unverified.

label.description: Optional human-readable label shown in the authenticator app and on the factor list (e.g. "iPhone 15").

enrollment.description: Type-specific enrollment payload. code.description: TOTP or emailed code (6 digits) OR a recovery code (16 hex chars, hyphenated or not). Emailed codes are requested via `/me/mfa/step-up/send-code` first. Omit when submitting `credential` instead.

credential.description: Passkey step-up: the `PublicKeyCredential` returned by `navigator.credentials.get()` against the options from `/me/mfa/step-up/webauthn/options`. Mutually exclusive with `code`.

factor_id.description: Email factor to deliver the code through. Defaults to the first enabled email factor on the account.

email_masked.description: Masked address the code was sent to.

account_id.description: End user who created (or last rotated) the key.

mfa_code_template_name.description: Mail template name fired when an email-type MFA factor needs a sign-in / step-up code delivered. Required (along with the master switch + sender) before email MFA factors can complete a challenge.

notifications_via_envoi.description: Master switch. When false (default) no notification mail goes out — customers handle email via webhooks. When true, every populated template slot fires through the workspace Mail domain.

password_reset_template_name.description: Mail template name fired when an end-user requests a password reset.

sender_mode.description: Where the From comes from. `workspace` (the default for new apps): the workspace default sender set in Mail, resolved at send time, so changing it in Mail changes it for every product. `custom`: `default_sender_address`. Sending `default_sender_address` without `sender_mode` sets `custom`.

verification_template_name.description: Mail template name fired when an end-user needs to verify their email. Must already exist in the workspace template store.

web_origin.description: Public origin of the customer's portal (e.g. `https://portal.dispute.markets`). Used to build clickable buttons in the verification + password-reset emails. Must be `https://host[:port]` or `http://localhost[:port]`; no path, no userinfo. Null clears the override and falls back to code-only delivery.

welcome_template_name.description: Mail template name fired right after an end-user verifies their email (welcome message).

enabled.description: `false` pauses export; `true` turns it back on and clears a stop after repeated failures. The position is kept either way: records written meanwhile are sent once export is on, within the audit log retention period.

url.description: New HTTPS address. The signing secret is kept (unlike `PUT`, which issues a new one). Changing it clears the receiver-test proof.

access_token_minutes.description: EndUser access-token lifetime in minutes (5-60, default 60). Independent of `session_duration_minutes`: the session and its refresh token can live for days while the access token expires in minutes. An access token is never issued for longer than the session it belongs to has left. M2M (client-credentials) tokens are unaffected and keep their fixed one-hour lifetime.

allowed_redirect_origins.description: Allowed origins for the `return_to` parameter on the OAuth web redirect callback. Exact origin match (scheme + host + port); no paths, no wildcards. Empty array disables the web redirect flow for this app. Prevents the callback from acting as an open-redirect.

enforce_app_permissions.description: When true, Consumer-API routes annotated with `@RequireAppPermission(perm)` enforce the requested perm against the EndUser's role-resolved permission set. When false (default), permission checks are bypassed — any valid token can call any annotated route. Flip on once you've authored roles + permissions for this app and want them to actually mean something.

max_failed_login_attempts.description: Consecutive failed signin attempts before an EndUser is locked out for 15 minutes. Applies to the signin lockout counters only; the separate short-burst limiter (5 attempts per identifier per minute) is fixed and not configurable.

max_sessions.description: Maximum concurrent sessions per EndUser. When a signin would take the account past this number, the OLDEST session — the one created longest ago, not the one used longest ago — is revoked (audited as `auth.session.evicted`). Omit or send null for unlimited.

mfa.description: Whether every EndUser must hold an MFA factor. `optional` (default) leaves MFA per-user opt-in. `required` refuses to mint a session for a user with no enabled factor: sign-in answers `{ mfa_enrollment_required: true, mfa_token, expires_at }` and the user enrols via POST /{app_slug}/v1/auth/mfa/enroll. IMPORTANT: turning this on does NOT terminate sessions that are already live — existing users keep their session until it expires or is revoked and only meet the requirement on their next sign-in. Revoke sessions explicitly if the policy has to bite immediately.

mfa_grace_days.description: Grace window in days, measured from ACCOUNT CREATION, during which `mfa: required` still mints ordinary tokens. The sign-in response then also carries `mfa_enrollment_due_at` so a client can prompt rather than block. 0 (default) means no grace. Note the anchor: an app that turns the policy on with existing users will find every account older than the window is already past it.

oauth_link_policy.description: How to handle a federated sign-in (Apple, Google, …) that lands on a verified email already belonging to an account in this app. `confirm` (default) refuses to auto-link and surfaces `link_required` so the user signs in with their original method. `auto` silently links when the provider claims the email is verified AND the email is not a private relay. `reject` refuses outright. Private-relay emails never auto-link regardless.

password_breach_check.description: Whether passwords are checked against a public breach corpus (HIBP Pwned Passwords, k-anonymity range API) before being accepted. `block` (default) rejects a breached password with 400 `PASSWORD_BREACHED`. `warn` accepts it and returns `password_warnings: ["breached"]` alongside the tokens. `off` disables the lookup entirely, so no outbound call is made. The lookup always fails open — a timeout or an unreachable corpus never blocks a signup. Only the first five characters of the password's SHA-1 ever leave the service.

password_require_uppercase.description: Require an uppercase letter in passwords.

session_duration_minutes.description: Session lifetime in minutes (1 minute to 30 days).

error.description: Failure code on `valid: false`. `TOKEN_INVALID` — signature / issuer / audience / app mismatch, an `end_user` token with no `sid` claim, or an `end_user` token whose account row no longer exists. `TOKEN_EXPIRED` — the token's own `exp` has passed. `TOKEN_REVOKED` — the backing session was revoked (sign-out, password change, admin revoke) or its row no longer exists because the end user was deleted. `SESSION_EXPIRED` — the session row is past `expires_at`; the access token outlived the session that minted it. `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` — the account exists but its status is not `active`.

post.description: Row fields: `email` (required), `username`, `display_name`, `role`, `tenant_slugs` (array), `external_id`, `metadata`, `email_verified`, and `password_hash` + `password_hash_algorithm`.  `password_hash_algorithm` is `argon2id` or `bcrypt`. **argon2id** hashes are accepted at any parameters. **bcrypt** hashes (`$2a$`, `$2b$`, `$2y$` — Auth0, PHP `password_hash`, Spring, node `bcrypt`, Devise / Rails, Laravel, Django) are accepted at any valid cost (4-31), verified on the user's first signin and replaced by an argon2id hash of the same password in that request, so the user keeps their password and never notices. Signin pads a bcrypt verify up to the argon2id floor, so at cost 10 and below an imported account cannot be told apart by timing; at cost 11 and above the verify is slower than the floor and answers when it finishes — a small timing difference on migrated accounts only, gone after each one's first signin.  A re-run is idempotent: rows match on `external_id` first, then the primary email, and update rather than duplicate. An existing password, an already-verified address and an existing member's role are never overwritten — see the module docs for why each one.
